To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we calculated the Debye mass in a plasma of light quarks coupled to a gluon background governed in mean-field approximation by a Polyakov loop potential and applied it to the description of the temperature-dependent singlet free energy at infinite separation for heavy quarks in QCD, which we compared to lattice data.

(i) the Debye mass is calculated in a plasma of quarks and gluons with the temporal gluon field governed by the Polyakow loop potential within the Polyakov loop Nambu Jona Lasinio model; and (ii) the Debye screening mass is used to describe the temperature dependence of lattice data for the singlet free energies of heavy quark pairs at infinite separation.

the screening of the quark potential in the PNJL plasma is described by a Debye mass that is suppressed in the confined phase and that this description of the Debye mass can be applied to the singlet free energies of heavy quarks at infinite separation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the screening of a static quark anti-quark pair by a quark plasma at finite temperature and chemical potential in the presence of a gluon Polyakov loop potential.
the calculation of the Debye screening mass in a quark plasma in the PNJL framework.
a study of the heavy quarks in a plasma of light quarks and gluons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Debye mass is not only a function of the temperature, but also of the chemical potential, which is not taken into account in the present work.
the PNJL Debye mass describes the singlet free energies well in the deconfined phase, but fails in the confined phase.
a phenomenological fit of the lattice data for the singlet free energies is not possible within the present PNJL model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can describe the singlet free energies of QCD with a pair of heavy quarks at infinite separation by the PNJL quasiparticle model with a Debye mass which is suppressed in the confined phase.
we have shown the importance of the Polyakov loop and the gluon background for the heavy quark pair potential in a quark plasma.
the PNJL quarks are not screened at all in the deconfined phase, but the screening of the quark potential in the confined phase can be described by the Polyakov potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple phenomenological model for the temperature dependence of a heavy quark potential can be obtained from the Debye mass of a quark plasma with the Polyakov loop.
the Debye mass calculated in the PNJL quasiparticle model agrees well with the lattice data.
the Debye mass is not a universal function of the Polyakov loop.
